key_insight: As doping and vacancy engineering in monolayer MoS2 tune the band structure and Fermi level, enabling either p-type or n-type behavior depending on defect type and site.
engineering_relevance: These defect-controlled electronic shifts suggest practical routes to optimize MoS2 for photocatalysis, photovoltaics, and FET device design.
method: DFT calculations on pristine and defected MoS2 monolayers
Compared Mo and S vacancies with As substitution at Mo/S sites and As interstitials
Analyzed structural changes and electronic density of states/Fermi-level shifts
evidence_signal: The abstract reports defect-induced midgap states and systematic Fermi-level shifts, with p-type behavior for vacancies and As substitution, and n-type behavior for As interstitial doping.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on first-principles modeling, so experimental validation is still needed to confirm defect stability and device performance under real fabrication conditions.
paper_title: First-principles study of the impact of As doping on the structural and electronic properties of MoS$_2$ monolayer
